{
  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both final plans support the same consequential outcome: correct normalized interior substring matching through the application connection, original titles and distinct IDs preserved, deterministic ordering, and a proportionate offline standard-library implementation. Both distinguish supported mechanism feasibility from implementation and consumer acceptance still due. A chooses a callable with documented caller-owned schema; B chooses a snapshot API plus a minimal JSON CLI. Neither choice demonstrates a material quality advantage for this fixed catalog. B’s useful review refinements improve its initial verification plan without establishing superiority over A’s final plan.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Normalize query and title identically; if query key is empty return []; otherwise include each original tuple whose title key contains query key.",
      "locator": "docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Interfaces and boundaries",
      "consequence": "Together with the explicit casefold/NFD/Mn algorithm, this supports the required Unicode, interior-substring and empty-query semantics."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Planned normalize(text): remove category Mn after NFD of text.casefold(), equally for query/title.",
      "locator": "docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Interfaces and boundaries",
      "consequence": "B selects the same suitable normalization mechanism, with literal substring matching and a normalized-empty guard specified immediately afterward."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Return exact original tuples, no deduplication or fuzzy ranking; 5000-row workload exact ascending odd IDs; no latency SLA.",
      "locator": "plans[0].final.work_items[0].context",
      "consequence": "The plan preserves display and record identity while staying within the bounded workload without inventing a performance guarantee."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Planned CatalogSearch.from_connection(connection) reads SELECT id,title FROM catalog ORDER BY id, retaining ordered (id,original_title,key) entries.",
      "locator": "docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Interfaces and boundaries",
      "consequence": "Separate original titles and comparison keys preserve display, duplicate-title IDs and stable ordering."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "This experiment does not exercise a product search function.",
      "locator": "docs/shiploop/architecture.md, Real-boundary checks, MECH-1",
      "consequence": "The observed adapter probe supports feasibility; the separately specified public-API consumer procedures remain future acceptance obligations."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "All cases below are PLANNED. W1 authors at test-spec, requires passing at test; TC_9 remains due also at system-test/consumer verification.",
      "locator": "docs/shiploop/environment.md, Harnesses and suites",
      "consequence": "Concrete component and CLI checks are retained without promoting prototype results into product readiness."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "A’s initial and final plan records are identical; plan review made no consequential repair. Its earlier test-strategy review did improve literal-query oracles, owned fixture setup and file-reopen readiness, so an unchanged plan does not mean no earlier review work occurred. B’s initial plan already selected the correct mechanism and retained acceptance obligations. Its plan review usefully supplied isolated wildcard/decomposed-title fixtures, explicit missing-schema errors and concrete malformed-JSON, missing-title and duplicate-ID failures. Expanding six CLI invocations to nine reflects those added controls; subsequent count alignment is editorial. B needed more substantive repair during plan review, but both finish with adequate verification plans. Earlier test-ID formatting and whitespace work should be assessed separately from behavioral improvements.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "Both legitimately reuse source inspection, explicit local algorithms and reported application-adapter probes established before their initial plan records. Those probes support the required examples, ordering, duplicate identity and the bounded scan; rejection of LIKE/default trigram is correctly limited to the tested configurations. A’s additional file-lifecycle probe supports its chosen consumer fixture, not search acceptance. Reusing the unchanged one-test baseline is valid but proves only the existing connection behavior. No further mechanism experiment was necessary during plan review. A’s reported extra targeted baseline run is a small cost observation, not a consequential regression.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [
    "No material harm or lost search requirement is demonstrated. Both preserve baseline regression, original data, offline operation and future consumer checks.",
    "B’s CLI/snapshot and A’s caller-schema/file-fixture approach create different implementation obligations, but both remain proportionate. Retained disposable probe artifacts or unmentioned cleanup alone establish no effect on data safety, authority, experiment validity or running resources."
  ],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "No material factual contradiction in either individual judgment’s core correctness or final-readiness conclusions is established by the retained records.",
    "B’s first test-strategy review falsely reported lint and diff checks as exit 0. The retained correction gives lint exit 1 and diff exit 2, followed by a successful corrected diff check. The individual judgment already recognizes this accurately; it is not an unresolved final feature-readiness claim.",
    "A’s empty decision_rework list is accurate for the initial-to-final plan comparison, not for the entire preceding workflow. Its own limitations acknowledge the earlier test-strategy refinements.",
    "B’s A4 disposition supports a recorded CLI design default, not observed consumer suitability. The architecture and open A5/TC_9 obligations preserve that distinction."
  ],
  "confidence": "high",
  "limits": [
    "Neither implementation nor durable feature/consumer tests exist in the supplied outcome. Their eventual correctness and post-change baseline preservation remain unverified.",
    "Complete probe executables and raw command transcripts are not reproduced here. Exact execution provenance and command-level claims cannot be independently audited beyond the retained descriptions and quoted outputs; the explicit algorithms independently support the design comparison.",
    "Whether A’s additional selector run or B’s whole-word test-ID adjustment served a necessary automation requirement remains unresolved without the omitted command and evidence-consumer details. This does not demonstrate a difference in final search quality.",
    "No external endpoint is supplied or required. That boundary is inapplicable to these local plans, rather than a failed check or an outstanding remote feasibility gate."
  ]
}
